[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Write Dobereiner’s law of Triads.","marks":1,"answer":"In a group of three elements showing the same kind of features, the atomic mass of the second element is half or near about half of the summation of the first’s and the third’s atomic mass. This is known as Dobereiner’s Law of Triads."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"“Chlorine is a halogen”–Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Halogen comes from Greek roots: ‘halo’ meaning salt and gen meaning ‘to produce’. As chlorine has the ability to form salts when it reacts with metals, chlorine is a halogen.
\[2Na + Cl_2 \rightarrow 2NaCl\]
\[Mg + Cl_2 \rightarrow MgCl_2\]
\[2Al + 3Cl_2 \rightarrow 2AlCl_3\]"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Find out the position of Y-element in the periodic table with the help of electronic configuration.","marks":3,"answer":"Atomic number of Y is 12. So, it is Mg.
\[Mg(12) \rightarrow 1s^2 \cdot 2s^2 \cdot 2p^6 \cdot 3s^2\]
It is s-block element. So, it’s group number will be determined only by the electron of last shell. As it has 2 electrons in the last shell, so it’s group is 2. The shell is 3, so it’s period is 3."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the sequence of atomic radius size of above mentioned three elements of stem.","marks":4,"answer":"Na(11), Mg(12) and Al(13) are situated in the 3rd period from right to left over in a period, the shell does not increase but the protons and electrons increase. So, the colombic attraction between nucleus and electrons increases. Thus the shells come close to the nucleus and the atomic radius of the element decreases. So, order of atomic radii–
\[X > Y > Z \text{ or, Na > Mg > Al}\]
---"}]

Rubidium (Rb) is an element of group-1 and it reacts with water produce strong alkali (rubidium hydroxide).
\[2Rb + 2H_2O \rightarrow 2RbOH + H_2\]
rubidium hydroxide (strong alkali)
This is why rubidium is called an alkali metal."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the group and period of the element ‘Y’ by electronic configuration.","marks":3,"answer":"Atomic number of Y is 9. So, it is fluorine (F).
\[F(9) \rightarrow 1s^2 \cdot 2s^2 \cdot 2p^5\]
The highest shell is 2. So, it's period is 2. It's last electro enters into P orbital. So, it is p-block element. That is why it's group number with be the sum of 10 and the number of electrons in the valence shell. Thus, Florine situated in the group \(7 + 10 = 17\)"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze why the order of ionization energies of the elements in the stem is not simply ascending.","marks":4,"answer":"The elements are—
\[\begin{array}{cccc}
U & (5) & B \\
V & (6) & C \\
W & (7) & N \\
X & (8) & O \\
Y & (9) & F \\
\end{array}\]
All are from 2nd period. By increasing atomic number, the ionization energy also increases.
So, the order should be \(B < C < N < O < F\) by general concept. But the N and O show exception. Nitrogen has stable configuration as p-orbital is half-filled.
N (7) \(\rightarrow\) 1s^2 \cdot 2s^2 \cdot 2p^3 (half-filled, so it is stable)
O (8) \(\rightarrow\) 1s^2 \cdot 2s^2 \cdot 2p^4 (Not half-filled, so it is not stable)
On the other and electronic configuration of oxygen is not stable. So, it requires more energy to get electron from nitrogen atom than oxygen atom. So, the order of ionization energy of the above elements is not ascending.
---"}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called metal?","marks":1,"answer":"Elements that can easily release electrons are called metals."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"What is meant by Mg\(^{2+}\)? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Mg\(^{2+}\) means Mg releases two electrons from its outermost energy shell and turns into divalent ion. Here, the electron number of Mg is 12 but after releasing 2 electrons, its electron number stands as 10. This is how Mg forms divalent ion or cation."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the order of electron affinity of 'A' and 'X'.","marks":3,"answer":"The energy emitted when we try to transform an element in its gaseous state into a 1 mole negative ion by injecting 1 mole electron into its one mole atom is called the electron affinity of that element.
The elements 'A' and 'X' of the stem are hydrogen (H) and helium (He) respectively.
The electronic configuration of H and He are-
\[H(1) \rightarrow 1s^1\]
\[He(2) \rightarrow 1s^2\]
From the electronic configuration we can see that, even if the 1s orbital of H is incomplete, the 1s orbital of He is complete. Thus, H may accept one electron but He does not tend to accept any electrons.
So, the electron affinity of He is considered as zero. Their order of electron affinity will be-
\[H > He.\]"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The ionization energy and atomic radius of 'Y' and 'Z' change inversely—Evaluate with logic.","marks":4,"answer":"The elements Y and Z of the stem is O and F respectively. These elements are situated at period-2 of the periodic table. The ionization energy and atomic radius of the elements are discussed below.
The energy that is required to transform an element into one mole positive ion by removing one mole electron from its one mole atom in its gaseous state is called the ionization energy of that element.
We know, in a period if moved from left to right, the sizes of the elements decreases. As a result, the attraction of the electrons of the outermost shell with the nucleus gradually becomes stronger. So, greater energy is required to remove electron. That means, if moved left to right in a period, the ionization energy of the elements increases. Therefore, the order of ionization energy of the 2\(^\text{nd}\) period: O<F.
Again, as we move from left to right in a period the atomic number gradually increases and the atomic radius gradually decreases. This is due to the addition of electrons with gradual increase of atomic number. But the number of energy level of the electron does not increase. As a result, the positive charge of nucleus increases. Thus, nucleus attracts electrons with greater energy and the atomic radius decreases. The order of atomic radius of the elements of stem: O > F.
So, it can be said that, the ionization energy and atomic radius of 'Y' and 'Z' i.e. O and F changes inversely.
---"}]

parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called duct rule?","marks":1,"answer":"Atoms of different elements exchange and share electrons with each other to obtain the arrangement of the helium atom is called the duct rule."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Fe\(^2+\) can act as both oxidant and reductant—Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"\[ \text{Fe}^{2+} \] ion accepts 2 electrons and is reduced to Fe atom. \[ \text{Fe}^{2+} + 2e \rightarrow \text{Fe}. \]
So, \[ \text{Fe}^{2+} \] is an oxidant.
On the other hand, \[ \text{Fe}^{2+} \] releases 1 electron and is oxidized to \[ \text{Fe}^{3+} \] ion.
\[ \text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + e; \] therefore, \[ \text{Fe}^{2+} \] is a reductant.
So, \[ \text{Fe}^{2+} \] ion works as both oxidant and reductant."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Find the position of ‘X’, ‘Z’ and ‘W’ elements in the periodic table according to the electronic configuration.","marks":3,"answer":"The elements \[ x_1 X_1, x_2 \text{and}_11 W \] of the stem are Sc, Si and Na respectively.
The electronic configuration of Sc-Sc(21) → \[ \text{Is}^2 \text{2s}^2 \text{2p}^6 \text{3s}^2 \text{3p}^6 \text{3d}^4 \text{4s}^2 \]
We know, if the outermost energy level of an element consists of s which is preceded by a d orbital in the inner level, the total number of electrons in those s and d orbitals is the group number of that element. Here, in the outermost energy level of Sc, there are 2 electrons in s shell and 1 electron in d shell. Therefore, group of Sc will be 2 + 1 = 3. Again, the period number is the number of outermost main energy level in the electronic configuration of that element. Then, in that case, the period number of Sc is 4.
Thus, Sc is situated at group 3 of period 4 of the modern periodic table.
The electronic configuration of Si-Si(14) → \[ \text{Is}^2 \text{2s}^2 \text{2p}^6 \text{3s}^2 \text{3p}^6 \]
From the electronic configuration, there are 3 orbits for the electronic configuration of silicon. So, silicon is in the 3rd period and since it is in the 3rd period so 10 is added to the electron number in the outermost shell to get group number 14.
Thus, Si is situated at group 14 of period 3 of the modern periodic table.
The electronic configuration of Na-Na(11) → \[ \text{Is}^2 \text{2s}^2 \text{2p}^6 \text{3s}^2 \]
The outermost electron is present in the 3rd energy level, so the period is 3. Again, if the electron enters only in the s-orbital, then the number of electrons in s-orbital will be the group number of the element. That means, the group number of Na is 1.
Thus, Na is situated at group 1 of period 3 of the modern periodic table."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the order of electron affinities and atomic radius of Y, Z, W elements.","marks":4,"answer":"The element \[ r_1 Y_1, r_2 Z \] and \[ n_1 W \] of the stem obtained in the order of atomic number of the elements present in the periodic table are Cl, Si and Na respectively. The energy emitted when we try to transform an element in its gaseous state into a 1 mole negative ion by injecting 1 mole electron into its one mole atom is called the electron affinity of that element.
From moving left to right in a period, the electron affinity increases gradually. Because, the atomic number gradually increases from left to right. As a result, the proton number of the nucleus increases as well as the positive charge; also, the number of electrons in the outermost shell increases. As a result, the attraction to the outer energy levels by the nucleus increases. Thus, the atomic size decreases. In this case, in the stem, the size of Na is the largest and the right-most element Cl has the smallest size. Thus, the atomic size of the element of this period is \[ \text{Na} > \text{Si} > \text{Cl}. \]
So the order of electron affinity of the elements will be \[ \text{Na} < \text{Si} < \text{Cl}. \]
---"}]

parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is mole?","marks":1,"answer":"The amount of a chemical substance that contains as many as the Avogadro number (6.02 × 10²³) of molecules, atoms or ions is called one mole of the substance."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"What do you mean by M/2 Na₂CO₃ solution?","marks":2,"answer":"M/2 Na₂CO₃ or 0.5 M Na₂CO₃ solution means at certain temperature 1 L solution contains 0.5 mol Na₂CO₃. The molecular mass of Na₂CO₃ is 106. That means if 53g or 0.5 mol Na₂CO₃ is dissolved in 1L solution, then that solution is called semimolar (M/2) Na₂CO₃ solution."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the position of element 'A' in the periodic table with the help of electronic configuration.","marks":3,"answer":"The atomic number of element A of the stem is 23. Therefore, the element A obtained in the order of atomic number of the elements present in the periodic table is Vanadium (V).
The electronic configuration of V is given below:
V (23) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d³ 4s²
Determination of Period: The number of the outermost main energy level in the electronic configuration of an element is the period number of that element. Here, the number of the outermost main energy level for V is 4. So, V is located at period 4.
Determination of Group: If the outermost energy level of an element consists of an s orbital which is preceded by a d-orbital in the inner level, the total number of electrons in those s and d orbitals is the group number of that element. Here, at the outermost energy level of V consists of s and is preceded by a d-orbital and they contain (3 + 2) = 5 electrons. So, the group number of V is 5.
Therefore, in the periodic table, V(23) is placed at period-4 group-5."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Electronic configuration of elements 'B' and 'C' are exceptional from general rule of electronic configuration.—Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"In the given stem, elements x₂B and x₃C have exceptional electronic configuration. Their atomic numbers are 24 and 29, respectively. So, these elements are Chromium (Cr) and Copper (Cu).
Their electron configurations are exceptional. Because:
If the orbitals of same energy are half-filled or full-filled then the electronic configuration is more stable. So, np³, np⁶, nd⁵, nd¹⁰, nf⁷, nf¹⁴ are more stable. And so, electron configuration of d⁵s¹ and d¹⁰s¹ is more stable than d⁴s² and d⁹s².
Electronic configuration of Cr(24)
Cr(24) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁵ 4s¹
In this configuration the 4s and 3d orbital are half-filled.
Similarly, electronic configuration of Cu(29)
Cu(29) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s¹
So, it can be said that the elements B and C of the stem, i.e. Cr and Cu has exceptional electronic configuration.
---"}]

The energy emitted when we try to transform an element in its gaseous state into a 1 mole negative ion by injecting 1 mole electron into its one mole atom is called the electron affinity of that element.
From moving left to right in a period, the electron affinity increases gradually. Because, the atomic number gradually increases from left to right. As a result, the proton number of the nucleus increases as well as the positive charge increases; also, the number of electrons in the outermost shell increases. As a result, the attraction of the outer energy levels by the nucleus increases. Thus, the atomic size decreases. So the order of electron affinity of the elements will be-Na <Al< Cl."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Though both of the elements ‘X’ and ‘Z’ are very reactive but their causes of reactivity are different.—Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"The element X and Z of the stem is Na and Cl respectively. Na is a metal while Cl is a non-metal. Both are elements of the 3\(^\text{rd}\) period of the periodic table.
The reactivity of a metal depends on its ionization energy. Metal with lower ionization energy is highly reactive. In the same period, while moving from right to left, the value of ionization energy decreases. As, Na is the left-most element in 3\(^\text{rd}\) period, it has the least amount of ionization energy and it is highly reactive as well.
Again, the reactivity of a non-metal depends on its electron affinity. In the same period, while moving from left to right, the value of electron affinityincreases. As, Cl is the right-most element in 3\(^\text{rd}\) period, it has the highest amount of electron affinity and it is highly reactive as well.
Therefore, it can be said that, despite of both Na and Cl being very reactive, the reason of Na reactivity is its lower ionization energy and the reactivity of Cl is due to higher electron affinity; that means the reasons of their reactivity is different.
---"}]

Position of Hydrogen: Hydrogen is a non-metal. However, the periodic table displays Hydrogen alongside strong electrophysic alkali metals like Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr etc. in group 1. It is because the outer shell of H contains only 1 electron like the alkali metals. Besides, many properties of Hydrogen are similar to those of the alkali metals. On the other hand, Hydrogen is also able to accept an electron like the halogen elements (F, Cl, Br, I), meaning it has some similarities with Halogens in terms of properties. So, it is only logical for the position H to be in group-1."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Does the electronic configuration of both ‘Y’ and ‘Z’ elements follow the general rules? Give logic in favour of your answer.","marks":4,"answer":"The elements Y and Z of the stem is Si(14) and Ag(47) respectively.
The electronic configuration of Si-Si(14) \(\rightarrow\) 1s\(^2\) 2s\(^2\) 2p\(^6\) 3s\(^2\) 3p\(^2\)
From the electronic configuration of Si we can see that, it follows the general rule of electronic configuration. But the electronic configuration of Ag(47) is an exception to the general electronic configuration rule.
Ag(47) \(\rightarrow\) 1s\(^2\) 2s\(^2\) 2p\(^6\) 3s\(^2\) 3p\(^6\) 3d\(^{10}\) 4s\(^2\) 4p\(^6\) 4d\(^{10}\) 5s\(^1\)
According to the general rule of electronic configuration, Ag should have had a configuration of 4d\(^7\) 5s\(^2\). But, in reality, its electronic configuration turned out to be 4d\(^{10}\) 5s\(^1\). The reason behind this exception is that orbital at the same energy level tends to be stable when they are either filled or half-filled. That means ns\(^1\), np\(^1\), nd\(^3\), nf\(^1\), ns\(^2\), np\(^6\), nd\(^{10}\), nf\(^{14}\) are the most stable. And this is also why the electronic configuration of d\(^{10}\)s\(^1\) and d\(^5\)s\(^1\) is much more stable than d\(^5\)s\(^2\) and d\(^5\)s\(^2\). In case of Ag, the same thing has happened. As 4d\(^{10}\) 5s\(^1\) electronic configuration is more stable than 4d\(^7\) 5s\(^2\), Silver's electronic configuration is an exception to the rule.
So, it can be said that, despite of Si following the general rule of configuration, it is different in case of Ag.
---"}]

According to Mendeleev’s periodic table, elements with lesser atomic mass were supposed to be set before the elements with higher atomic mass. The electronic configuration of Li, K, Mg and Al are as follows:
Li (3) \(\rightarrow\) 1s\(^2\) 2s\(^1\)

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Write down the Mendeleev's periodic law.","marks":1,"answer":"Mendeleev's periodic law: Physical and chemical properties of elements return periodically as atomic mass of elements increase."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is CO₃²⁻ called radical? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Sometimes a bundle of atoms from more than one element combine together, by receiving positive and negative charges and acting as an ion of an element. They are called radicals.
CO₃²⁻ is called a radical because one carbon atom and three oxygen atoms combine together but acts as a single ion in a chemical reaction."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which one is more active between the elements 'W' and 'Z' of the stem? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"In the stem, the element denoted W is sodium (Na) and Z is potassium (K).
The electronic configuration of Na and K are as follows:
Na (11) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s¹
K (19) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s¹
Here, Na and K are both elements of group 1 or alkali group. From the periodic property, we know that, as the elements progress from top to bottom, their atomic size increases. For this, the attraction between the nucleus and the outermost electron becomes less with the increase of distance. Therefore, the ionization energy and electron affinity decreases as the elements progress from top to bottom.
From these characteristics mentioned above, we can see that, the atomic radius of Na is less than K, so the ionization energy of Na is more than K. Hence, K will donate electron more easily than Na and thus, will be more active."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the order of the ionization energy of W, X and Y elements.","marks":4,"answer":"In the stem, the element denoted W is sodium (Na), X is sulphur (S), and Y is argon (Ar).
Na, S, and Ar are the elements in the period 3. We know that, the energy that is required to transform an element into one mole positive ion removing one mole electron from its one mole atom in its gaseous state is called the ionization energy. It is a periodic property and it increases with decrease in the radius of the atom.
We know that, in the same period, the elements of the left side have greater radius than those on the right side. Being in the same period, Na is the left most element and Ar is the right most element of that period. Therefore, the radius of Na will be largest and Ar will be smallest in this period. S is third from the right in the periodic table. So, its radius will be greater than Ar but smaller than Na. So the order of the ionization energy of these elements is:
Na < S < Ar.
---"}]

Atomic radius decreases across a period because similar number of shells bit one electron and proton is added by successive element. So the force of attraction between the nucleus and the outermost shell increases. So atomic radius decreases.

So, the element is Chromium (Cr).
The electronic configuration of Cr, \(_2\text{Cr} \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^5 4s^1\)
The electronic configuration above has one electron in the outermost level which is in the s orbital and it is preceded by a d orbital in the inner level. Therefore, the total number of electrons in those s and d orbitals is the group number of that element. On the other hand, the maximum number of shells where the electrons have entered is the period of that element.
As the total number of electrons in those s and d orbital of Cr is 1+5 = 6, therefore, Cr is in group-6. And the maximum number of shell is 4, where the electrons have entered, therefore, Cr is in period-4."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the order of ionization energy of elements A, B and C mentioned in the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"The atomic numbers of elements A, B, and C in the stem are 8, 13, and 16. So, the elements are Oxygen (O), Aluminium (Al), and Sulphur (S).
The electronic configurations of the elements are as follows:
\[_1\text{O} \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^4\]
\[_1\text{Al} \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^1\]
\[_1\text{S} \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^1\]
The energy required to transform an element into one mole positive ion by removing one mole electron from its one mole atom in its gaseous state is called the ionization energy of that element. In the same period, elements of the left side have greater radius than those of the right side. When the atomic radius is less, the ionization energy is more and vice-versa. In the same group, elements of the top has lower atomic radius then that of the bottom, because one extra shell is added each time a period increases.
Here, we can see from the electronic configuration, O and S are in group-16 and Al is in group-13. On the other hand, O is in period 2 but Al and S are in period-3. Here, O has the lowest atomic radius because it has one less shell than the other two. So the ionization energy of O will be the highest among these three. Then, between Al and S, S is closer to the nearest inert gas than Al, so the radius of S is less than Al. Therefore, the ionization energy of S is higher than Al. Thus, the order of ionization energy among these three elements will be: O > S > Al.
---"}]

And the energy emitted when we try to transform an element in its gaseous state into one mole negative ion by injecting one mole electron into its one mole atom is called the electron affinity of that element.
In the same period, elements of the left side have greater radius than those of the right side. When the atomic radius decreases, the ionization energy increases and vice versa. So, the order of the ionization energy of the elements given in the stem is: \( Na < Mg < P < S \). Electron affinity also increases if the radius of the atom decreases. Bronze is made by mixing molten copper and tin, and then cooling the mixture. As it is made by two metals copper and tin, therefore bronze is an alloy."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the position of elements in periodic table which are mentioned in group-2 of the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The elements of group 2 of the stem denoted by ⁸⁵M, ⁸⁸Q, and ¹⁹R are ²⁷Co, ³⁸Sr, and ⁹F, where the numbers represent atomic numbers of the elements.
The electronic configurations are given below:
Cobalt (²⁷Co) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁷ 4s²
Strontium (³⁸Sr) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p⁶ 5s²
Fluorine (⁹F) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁵
In case of cobalt, the number of the outermost energy level is 4 and the electrons are in s orbital which is preceded by a d orbital. Therefore, the period number of Co is 4. We know, if the outermost energy level of an element consists of an s orbital which is preceded by a d orbital in the inner level, the total number of electrons in those s and d orbitals is the group number of that element. The total number of electrons in 4s and 3d orbital is (2+7) = 9. So, the position of Co is group-9, period-4.
In case of strontium, the number of the outermost energy level is 5 and the electrons are in s orbital only. Therefore, the period number of Sr is 5. We know that if the outermost energy level of an element consists of s orbital only, the total number of electrons in that s orbital is the group number of that element. As, the 5s orbital of Sr has 2 electrons, so the group number of Sr is 2. So, the position of Sr is group-2, period-5.
In case of fluorine, the number of the outermost energy level is 2 and the electrons are in s and p orbitals. Therefore, the period number of F is 2. We know that if the outermost energy level of an element consists of s and p orbitals only, the total number of electrons in those s and p orbitals added with 10 is the group number of that element. So the group number of F is (2 + 5 + 10) = 17. So, the position of F is group-17, period-2."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the series of atomic radius of group-1 elements mentioned in the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"The elements of group 1 of the stem denoted by ¹³X, ¹⁴Y, and ³¹Z are ¹³Al, ¹⁴Si, and ³¹Ga, where the numbers represent the atomic number of the elements.
The electronic configurations are given below:
Aluminium (¹³Al) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p¹
Silicon (¹⁴Si) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p²
Gallium (³¹Ga) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p¹
From the electronic configuration, we can say that, Al and Ga are in group-13 and Si is in group-14. Moreover, Al and Si are in period 3 whereas Ga in period 4.
From the characteristics of the periodic table, we know that, the size of an atom or the atomic radius decrease as the period progresses from left to right. The reason is, in a period, the more we move from left to right, the atomic number increases, but the shell number remains unchanged. The proton number also increases with the atomic number and so do the number of electrons. Therefore, the attraction between the increased number of electrons and protons also increases, resulting in electron containing shells getting closer to the nucleus. As a result, the atomic radius decreases. Again, in the same group, the lower we move from the upper part, a new shell is added to the outer layer. These added shells increase the radius of an atom.
Therefore, the order of the atomic radius is: Si < Al < Ga.
---"}]

Hence, their respective electronic configuration can be written as:

All three elements given in the stem can be found in group 17 of the periodic table. The period number of element A, B and C is 2, 3 and 4 respectively. This happens because down a group, the number of energy levels (n) increases, so there is a greater distance between the nucleus and the outermost orbital. This results in a larger atomic radius. Therefore, the order of atomic radius is: F < Cl < Br."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Electronic configuration is the main basis of periodic table.—Analyze it by the help of the elements of stem.","marks":4,"answer":"According to the stem, element A, B, and C are Fluorine, Chlorine and Bromine respectively. ₉F → 1s² 2s² 2p⁵
₁₇Cl → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁵
₃₅Br → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p⁵
We know that electronic configuration helps to identify the group and period of an element in the periodic table. Elements having the same number of electrons in its outermost shell is placed in one group. This can be verified by looking at the electronic configuration of F, Cl and Br written above. It can be observed that the outermost energy level of all three elements is s²p⁵.

Atomic Radius: We know, as we go down from top to bottom in a period, one energy level is added to the atoms. That is atomic radius increases. So the order of increase of atomic radius of the period A of the stem will be,

It is placed in group-1 and He is placed in group-18. Whether the positioning of the elements H and He are correct or not is analysed as follows—
Alkali metals like Li, Na, K, Rb etc. have one valence electron like Hydrogen. For example,
\[ Li (3) = 1s^2 \left[ \frac{2s}{3} \right] \]
\[ Na (11) = 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 \left[ \frac{3s}{3} \right] \]
\[ H(1) = \left[ \frac{1s}{3} \right] \]
Like alkali metals, H is also electro-positive: as a result, it can easily donate an electron and convert into a hydrogen ion or proton (H\(^+\)). Like,
\[ Na \rightarrow Na^+ + e^-, H \rightarrow H^+ + e^- \]
Like alkali metals, hydrogen also combines with negatively charged halogen to form halide. For example: NaCl, HCl. The molten liquid of alkali metal halide, for example, NaCl is electrolysed then Na will deposit at the cathode. Similarly, if HCl solution is electrolysed, then H\(_2\) will be deposited at the cathode. Hydrogen is a strong reductant similar to any alkali metal or any other metal. But many characteristics of H coincide with the halogens as well. But as most of the characteristics match alkali metals, H is placed in group-1.
For these reasons, despite of being a non-metal, H is not placed in group-17 but in group-1.
Electronic configuration of \( \frac{4}{2} \) He is - \( 1s^2 \). According to the electronic configuration, He should be placed with the elements of group-2. The elements of group-2 are chemically reactive, but He is chemically inert. Each element of group-2 has 2 electrons in the valence shell (ns\(^2\)) which is incomplete, but He is completed with 2 electrons in its valence shell (1s\(^2\)). Thus, the properties of He match with the inert gases of group-18 like Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe. The elements of group-2 are alkaline earth metals and their valency is 2. He never behaves like the extremely positive alkaline earth metals. For this reason, He was not placed in group-2 but in group-18.
Therefore, in the above period, the position of A and X is correct.
---"}]

Write down with example.","marks":2,"answer":"Aufbau principle states that the electron always enters the orbital with the least amount of energy in the ground state of an atom.
That means electrons will enter the lowest energy level first and the highest level later. The energy level of orbital is determined by the summation of value of the principal energy level (n) and value of energy sublevel (l). The orbital that has lesser value of (n + l) is of lesser energy level and it gets the first entry of electron. The orbital that has a higher value of (n + l) is of higher energy level and it gets the later entry of electron.
Electron configuration of potassium-
K(19 = 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^1
For 3d orbital, n = 3 and l = 2, so the value (n + l) becomes (3 + 2 = 5). Again, for 4s, n = 4 and l = 0, so the value (n + l) becomes (4 + 0 = 4). It shows 4s orbital has a lower energy than 3d orbital. Therefore, electrons will first enter 4s and then will go to 3d."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine period and group of the element (i) and (ii).","marks":3,"answer":"Element (i) is potassium and element (ii) is chromium.
Determining the Period Number: The number of the outermost main energy level in the electronic configuration of an element is the period number of that element. the electronic configuration of K(19) = 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^1. Since the outermost energy level of potassium is the fourth one, so the element belongs to period 4 of the table. Same way, the electronic configuration of Chromium is Cr(24) = 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^4 4s^2. Since the outermost energy level of chromium is the fourth one, the element belongs to period 4 of the table.
Determining the Group:
For Potassium: If the outermost energy level of an element consists of s orbital only, the total number of electrons in that s orbital is the group number of that element. The electronic configuration of K(19) = 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^1. Since the outermost energy level of potassium consists of s orbital and it contains only 1 electron, so the element belongs to the group 1 of the table.
For Chromium: If the outermost energy level of an element consists of s orbital which is preceded by d orbital in the inner level, the total number of electrons in those s and d orbital is the group number of that element. The electronic configuration of Cr(24) = 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^4. Since the outermost energy level of chromium consists of s and is preceded by d orbital and they contain 4 + 2 = 6 electrons, so the element belongs to the group 6 of the table."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"“The order of electron affinity of chlorine is greater than that of sulfur”-Analyze it logically.","marks":4,"answer":"The energy emitted when we try to transform an element in its gaseous state into a 1 mole negative ion by injecting 1 mole electron into its one mole atom is called the electron affinity of that element.
The atomic number of sulfur (S) is 16 and that of chlorine (Cl) is 17. In the periodic table, both the elements are placed in period-3. And if we progress from left to right in a period, the atomic number increases. As the atomic number increases, the number of protons also increases. So the nuclear positive charge increases. And as the nuclear positive charge increases, its tendency to attract more electrons increases. So, the tendency to accept electrons increases. As a result, the order of electron affinity is S < Cl.

## Question 21:
A → nd⁵(n+1)s²
B → (n-1)s²(n-1)p⁵
C → ns²np⁵

parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is isotope?","marks":1,"answer":"Atoms of the same element with an equal number of protons but different numbers of neutrons and mass are called isotopes of each other."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"f-orbital is not possible in 3rd shell—why?","marks":2,"answer":"In the 3rd energy level, electrons occupy only the s, p, and d sublevels.
We have seen all energy levels are specified with n. These levels are again divided into sublevels which are expressed by l. The value of l is from 0 to n-1. These sublevels are called orbital. They are identified with s, p, d, f etc. When n = 3, l = 0, 1, 2. There will be three orbitals: 3s, 3p, 3d. That's why f orbital is not possible in 3rd shell."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the bond formation between A & C of the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"Bond formation between A and C is due to ionic bond.
Ionic bonding is the complete transfer of valence electrons between atoms and is a type of chemical bond that generates two oppositely charged ions. Metals have only a few electrons in its outermost orbital. By losing those electrons, these metals can achieve noble-gas configuration and satisfy the octet rule. Similarly, nonmetals that have close to 8 electrons in its valence shell tend to easily accept electrons to achieve its noble gas configuration.
Here, A is Calcium (3d⁰ 4s²) and C is Chlorine (3s² 3p⁵). The calcium atom donates two electrons from its outermost energy level in order to get the configuration like argon and produces calcium cation (Ca²⁺). Two Cl atoms accept one electron each to reach the electronic configuration of argon (Ar) gas and thus produce chloride (Cl⁻) ions. These mutually opposite charges are attracted towards each other by electrostatic force. This attraction force is ionic bond. In other words, in the chemical bonding between a metal and a non-metal, the bond that is formed when the elements turn into positive and negative ions is called the ionic bond. The compound that has ionic bond is called ionic compound (CaCl₂).
Ca → Ca²⁺ + 2e⁻
2Cl + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻
Ca + 2Cl → Ca²⁺ + 2Cl⁻ → CaCl₂"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"The elements B and C of the stem are of same group in the periodic table—prove it based on their chemical properties.","marks":4,"answer":"Element B is Fluorine (2s² 2p⁵) and element C is Chlorine (3s² 3p⁵).
Electron configuration of F(9) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁵ and Cl(17) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁵. They both belong to same group-17. The gases F₂ and Cl₂ react with Hydrogen and produce HF (g) and HCl (g) gases respectively.
H₂(g) + F₂(g) → 2HF(g)
H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2HCl(g)
Again, if we dissolve these gases into water, they produce hydrohalide acids, i.e. Hydrofluoric acid and Hydrochloric acid.
HF(g) + H₂O(l) → HF(aq)
HCl(g) + H₂O(l) → HCl(aq)
These hydrohalide acids react with any carbonate salt and produce Carbon dioxide gas. For example, Calcium Carbonate and Hydrofluoric acid produce Carbon dioxide:
CaCO₃ + 2HF(aq) → CaF₂ + CO₂ + H₂O
Similarly, Calcium Carbonate and Hydrochloric acid also produce Carbon dioxide:
CaCO₃ + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂ + CO₂ + H₂O
These similar chemical properties prove that elements B and C belong to the same group in the periodic table."}]
